claims.head: Expect the Lightning to fire from everywhere

claims.head: The Lightning’s edge in shots from defensemen
claims.body: The Lightning are near the top of the league for shots from defensemen, and the Kraken are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

notes.text: Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, up from 2% last season.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 5 of their last 6 games, including the last one. Gage Goncalves takes shifts on two lines, L1 and L4. Victor Hedman is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Černák and Crozier.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 38% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 26 seconds at a time, against 66 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (9 of 13 changes).

TBL.head: The Lightning should be in control
TBL.body: Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Kraken’s best way in is keeping dangerous shots away.

SEA.head: The Lightning should be favored
SEA.body: Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Kraken’s best hope is keeping dangerous shots away, plus a big night in goal.
